metadata.title: Quarterly microcomputer market share
metadata.status: Alternative-history unit-shipment scenario; quarterly market totals are modelled, not observed
metadata.scope: Worldwide microcomputer unit shipments; Logix includes UK distributor shipments. Five clone brands counted only for their compatible product lines. Other legacy products of those brands remain in other manufacturers.

methodology.definition: Complete microcomputers, including home/business models; exclude peripherals, terminals, upgrades and software. Shipment-unit share, not revenue or installed-base share.
methodology.basis: 1981/1982 contemporaneous Dataquest estimates reported by TIME; scope comparability is approximate. 1983 round planning assumption, not a sourced historical count. Quarterly allocation 21/23/25/31 is modelled, not observed. Add only 20% of Logix+clone demand to the calibrated market; the remainder displaces other suppliers.
methodology.source_title: TIME, The Computer Moves In, January 1983
methodology.1980_basis: 1.1m worldwide planning denominator for added 1980 views; not a sourced historical total.

manufacturers.name: Other manufacturers and legacy product lines

methodology.definition: Disk-equipped computers bought for business use, worldwide; exclude home/education purchases even if disk-equipped. All modelled Logix/clone systems allocated to business for this segment estimate.
methodology.basis: Illustrative addressable-market assumptions, not observed counts. All-vendor retail datasets do not establish business-use classification. 20% of platform volume expands baseline; remainder displaces competitors. Rival weights distribute only residual business demand.
